copy_discriminant.descriptive_result: The same-byte fresh-inode copy roles have materially lower executable-file RSS and GNU time peaks than original-path roles in this capture. Within copies, after-copy is close to or below before-copy; the large original-path before/after executable RSS difference is not reproduced by the copy roles.
copy_discriminant.interpretation_limit: This is consistent with a pathname/inode/file-residency association in these runs, but copy cache state, ASLR, and non-atomic observer sampling prevent a precise kernel mechanism claim. It is not a latency or adoption experiment.

interpretive_status: descriptive diagnostic; no candidate adoption decision
mapping_breakdown_findings: Original diagnostic sampled executable-file RSS is concentrated in r-xp: role median bands are 14692-14716 KiB before and 17152-17336 KiB after. The corresponding r--p mapping includes approximately 240-248 KiB Private_Dirty/Anonymous COW bytes; filename RSS is therefore not all clean file residency.

Heap, stack, and unlabelled anonymous mapping RSS do not show a matching increase: original role median bands are approximately heap 1600-1776 KiB, stack 628-632 KiB, anonymous 48 KiB; after values are heap 1512-1612 KiB, stack 628-632 KiB, anonymous 48-52 KiB.

All sampled aggregate FilePmdMapped and AnonHugePages values are zero, and every parsed VMA reports 4 KiB KernelPageSize and MMUPageSize. The captures provide no evidence of a transparent huge-page or large-folio mapping, while not proving that no kernel cache or fault-around mechanism exists.
scope: Independent replay of every raw status/smaps JSONL line from the eight-child original diagnostic and sixteen-child copy probe. GNU time peaks, status samples, and smaps samples remain separate.
